title: Applying a decoded transition record
statement: Let $M$ be a coded machine, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be Boolean words, let $\mathrm{src}$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, let $p$ and $p_0$ be natural numbers, and let $a$ be any action for $M$. One step of the universal interpreter from the evaluation configuration built from the simulation configuration of $\mathrm{src}$ at table position $p_0$, with the record-application control carrying the eight bits of $a$ and its halting flag, table $M$'s serialization at cursor $p$, and the unary state tape for $a$'s successor state, equals the simulation configuration of the result of applying $a$ to $\mathrm{src}$ at table position $p$.
replaced:
Let $M$ be a coded machine, let $\mathrm{src}$ be a configuration of $M$, and
let $a$ be a transition action of $M$.  One step of the (unstopped) four-tape
table interpreter from the pending-action evaluation configuration --- built
over the interpreter checkpoint of $\mathrm{src}$, carrying the eight decoded
bits of $a$ and the halting flag of its successor, with the serialized table,
any table cursor $p$, and the unary tape of the successor index installed ---
equals exactly the interpreter checkpoint of the configuration obtained by
applying $a$ to $\mathrm{src}$, with table cursor $p$; this includes the
correct virtual-input head movement, optional write, emission, and the halting
case.
